Maya: Quick heads-up users hitting confusion: py SDK throws bare Exception on auth/rate-limit, e.g. `Exception: Request failed (status=401)` with no structured fields.
Ravi: Oof. Which version?
Maya: 0.9.2 in quickstart. The error only has .args. No http_status or retryable.
Ola: We added typed errors to js last quarter; py parity would help.
Maya: Proposal: introduce ApiError with fields `http_status`, `error_kind` (enum string), `retryable` (bool), optional `retry_after` (int), and set `__cause__` to the original requests exception. Backwards-compatible pattern.
Ravi: Agree. Also include `details` string for server messages. Add helper `should_retry(method)` that considers idempotency.
Ola: Docs should include mapping table: 401->Unauthorized (retryable=false), 403->Forbidden(false), 404->NotFound(false), 409->Conflict(false/depends), 429->RateLimit(true), 500-599->ServerError(true/depends).
Maya: I'll open a py SDK draft PR that implements ApiError + tests and updates quickstart sample to catch ApiError and branch on `retryable`.
ci-bot: ci: py-sdk/tests mapping_tests passed at 2024-11-15T11:03:05Z
Ravi: Add MIGRATION.md note and changelog. Also small lint to remind to `raise ApiError(...) from original_exc` when wrapping.
Ola: I'll update quickstart snippet and include an example showing `except ApiError as e: if e.retryable: backoff()` so new users can follow.
Maya: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/py-sdk/pull/236 (draft). Thanks team.
